summary: The LLM landscape in late 2026 is defined by intense competition among proprietary frontier models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, alongside a surging wave of high-quality open-weight models from DeepSeek, Alibaba (Qwen), and others. Enterprise consumption increasingly flows through cloud aggregators like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, which dramatically amplifies real-world adoption beyond direct-API figures. While GPT-series models retain the largest overall usage and web traffic, Anthropic's Claude has posted the fastest growth, and open models dominate HuggingFace downloads and self-hosted developer deployments.

models.name: GPT-5.x (GPT-5 / GPT-5.1 series)
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT recorded 5.32 billion web visits (far ahead of all rivals), and OpenAI models top the Shakudo top-9 ranking while being broadly available via Azure OpenAI and aggregators.
models.best_for: General-purpose production applications requiring a reliable, well-supported frontier model

models.name: Claude Opus 5.5 / Claude (Sonnet, Opus) series
models.popularity_notes: Claude Opus 5.5 ranks #1 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (score 58), grew 452% YoY in audience, and is available across AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex.
models.best_for: Complex coding, agentic tasks, and enterprise applications needing top reasoning quality

models.name: Gemini 2.x series
models.popularity_notes: Gemini ranked second in web traffic with 1.14 billion visits and is natively distributed through Google Vertex AI with massive enterprise reach.
strengths: Deep Google Cloud / Vertex AI integration
models.best_for: Multimodal and long-document workloads within the Google Cloud ecosystem

models.name: DeepSeek (V3 / R1 series)
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek is the highest-ranked open-weight challenger per the Facebook traffic data and ranks #2 in Shakudo's top-9, dominating HuggingFace downloads and cost-sensitive self-hosted deployments.
models.best_for: Cost-efficient self-hosted deployments and reasoning tasks at scale

models.name: Qwen (Qwen3 series)
models.popularity_notes: Qwen ranks #3 in Shakudo's top-9 and is among the most downloaded open-weight model families on HuggingFace, with broad adoption in Asia and growing aggregator availability.
models.best_for: Multilingual applications and flexible open-weight fine-tuning

models.name: Llama (Llama 4 series)
models.popularity_notes: Llama remains the most-deployed open-weight base for enterprise fine-tuning and is offered across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, IBM watsonx, and Snowflake Cortex.
models.best_for: Enterprise-grade open-weight customization and private deployments

models.name: Grok (Grok 4 series)
models.popularity_notes: Grok ranks #4 in Shakudo's top-9 with rapidly growing developer adoption driven by X integration and competitive frontier performance.
models.best_for: Applications needing real-time information and conversational reasoning

models.name: GLM (GLM-4.x series)
models.popularity_notes: GLM ranks #5 in Shakudo's top-9 and has strong open-weight adoption on HuggingFace, especially for coding and agentic tasks at low cost.
models.best_for: Cost-effective open-weight coding and agent development

models.name: Nemotron (Nemotron series)
models.popularity_notes: Nemotron ranks #7 in Shakudo's top-9 and is distributed via NVIDIA NIM and cloud aggregators, with strong enterprise adoption for GPU-optimized inference.
models.best_for: GPU-accelerated enterprise inference and NVIDIA-stack deployments

models.name: Mistral (Mistral Large / Mixtral series)
models.popularity_notes: Mistral maintains broad developer adoption through open weights and availability on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, IBM watsonx, and Snowflake Cortex.
models.best_for: European and privacy-focused enterprises needing open-weight flexibility
